/-- A flat, formally unramified algebra, essentially of finite type over a domain, is reduced.
This generalizes `Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field` from fields to domains, at the
price of the flatness assumption (which is automatic over a field). -/
theorem Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
    [IsDomain B] [Algebra B S] [Algebra.FormallyUnramified B S] [Algebra.EssFiniteType B S]
    [Module.Flat B S] : IsReduced S := by
  have : IsReduced (FractionRing B ⊗[B] S) :=
    Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_field (FractionRing B) (FractionRing B ⊗[B] S)
  refine isReduced_of_injective
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := B) (A := FractionRing B) (B := S)) ?_
  have h : ⇑(Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := B) (A := FractionRing B) (B := S)) =
      ⇑(LinearMap.rTensor S (Algebra.ofId B (FractionRing B)).toLinearMap) ∘
        ⇑(TensorProduct.lid B S).symm := by
    ext s
    simp
  rw [h]
  exact (Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _
    (IsFractionRing.injective B (FractionRing B))).comp (TensorProduct.lid B S).symm.injective

/-- An étale algebra over a domain is reduced. -/
theorem Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S] [IsDomain B]
    [Algebra B S] [Algebra.Etale B S] : IsReduced S :=
  Algebra.FormallyUnramified.isReduced_of_isDomain B S

/-- The target of a standard smooth ring homomorphism out of a domain is reduced: by
Stacks 00T7 it is étale over a polynomial ring over the base, and étale algebras over
domains are reduced. -/
theorem RingHom.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain {B S : Type*} [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
    [IsDomain B] {g : B →+* S} (hg : g.IsStandardSmooth) : IsReduced S := by
  obtain ⟨n, φ, -, hφ⟩ := hg.exists_etale_mvPolynomial
  algebraize [φ]
  exact Algebra.Etale.isReduced_of_isDomain (MvPolynomial (Fin n) B) S

/-- A standard smooth algebra over a domain is reduced. -/
theorem Algebra.IsStandardSmooth.isReduced_of_isDomain (B S : Type*) [CommRing B] [CommRing S]
    [IsDomain B] [Algebra B S] [Algebra.IsStandardSmooth B S] : IsReduced S :=
  (RingHom.isStandardSmooth_algebraMap.mpr ‹_›).isReduced_of_isDomain

end RingTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

open CategoryTheory Limits

variable {X Y : Scheme.{u}}

/-- A scheme smooth over the spectrum of a field is reduced. -/
theorem Smooth.isReduced_of_field {K : Type u} [Field K] (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of K)) [Smooth f] :
    IsReduced X := by
  have hsub : Subsingleton (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
  choose U hU V hV hxV e hsm using Smooth.exists_isStandardSmooth f
  -- Each chart is the spectrum of a standard smooth algebra over (a ring isomorphic to) `K`,
  -- hence reduced.
  have hred (x : X) : IsReduced (V x).toScheme := by
    have : IsAffine (V x).toScheme := hV x
    have hfx : f x ∈ U x := e x (hxV x)
    have hUx : U x = ⊤ := by
      refine TopologicalSpace.Opens.ext (Set.eq_univ_of_forall fun y ↦ ?_)
      exact Subsingleton.elim (f x) y ▸ hfx
    have hdom : IsDomain Γ(Spec (CommRingCat.of K), U x) := by
      rw [hUx]
      exact Function.Injective.isDomain
        (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (CommRingCat.of K)).commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv (RingEquiv.injective _)
    have hΓ : _root_.IsReduced Γ(X, V x) := (hsm x).isReduced_of_isDomain
    have : _root_.IsReduced Γ((V x).toScheme, ⊤) :=
      isReduced_of_injective (V x).topIso.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv (RingEquiv.injective _)
    exact isReduced_of_isAffine_isReduced _
  let 𝒰 : X.OpenCover := Scheme.Cover.mkOfCovers X (fun x ↦ (V x).toScheme) (fun x ↦ (V x).ι)
    (fun x ↦ ⟨x, ⟨x, hxV x⟩, rfl⟩) (fun x ↦ inferInstance)
  have : ∀ i, IsReduced (𝒰.X i) := hred
  exact IsReduced.of_openCover _ 𝒰

/-- A smooth morphism of schemes is geometrically reduced: every base change to the spectrum
of a field is smooth over that field, hence reduced. -/
instance (priority := 100) Smooth.geometricallyReduced (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f] :
    GeometricallyReduced f where
  geometrically_isReduced := fun K _ y Z fst snd h ↦
    have : Smooth snd := MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @Smooth) h ‹Smooth f›
    Smooth.isReduced_of_field snd

/-- A morphism smooth of relative dimension `1` is smooth. This is the relative dimension of
the curve bundle of the Jacobian challenge; the general statement is
`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth`, which cannot be an instance since `n` does not occur in
the conclusion. -/
instance (priority := 100) Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] : Smooth f :=
  SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth 1 f

/-- A morphism smooth of some relative dimension is geometrically reduced. Not an instance
since `n` cannot be inferred from the conclusion; for relative dimension `1`, instance
resolution goes through `Smooth.of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one`. -/
theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyReduced (n : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f] : GeometricallyReduced f :=
  have : Smooth f := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth n f
  inferInstance

/-- A smooth, geometrically irreducible morphism is geometrically integral. -/
instance (priority := 100) Smooth.geometricallyIntegral (f : X ⟶ Y) [Smooth f]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible f] : GeometricallyIntegral f :=
  .of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible f

/-- A geometrically irreducible morphism, smooth of some relative dimension, is geometrically
integral. Not an instance since `n` cannot be inferred from the conclusion. -/
theorem SmoothOfRelativeDimension.geometricallyIntegral (n : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y)
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f] [GeometricallyIrreducible f] : GeometricallyIntegral f :=
  have : Smooth f := SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth n f
  .of_geometricallyReduced_of_geometricallyIrreducible f

section CurveBundle

/-! Instance-resolution smoke tests for the hypothesis bundle of the Jacobian challenge
(the `IsProper` hypothesis is omitted as it plays no role here): the curve `C` is
geometrically reduced and geometrically integral, by `inferInstance`. -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

example : GeometricallyReduced C.hom := inferInstance
example : GeometricallyIntegral C.hom := inferInstance

end CurveBundle

end AlgebraicGeometry

1	# Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2	
3	A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4	irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5	the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6	abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7	property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8	the open frontier.
9	
10	Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11	`Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12	descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13	The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14	The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15	being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16	expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17	Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18	sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.
19	
20	It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
21	same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.
22	
23	## State (measured 2026-07-27)
24	
25	- **172 modules, 124,300 lines.**  **26 `sorry`** remain, spread over 11 modules;
26	  the rest are locally sorry-free.
27	- A warm `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` is **green**: 8,723 jobs, exit 0.
28	- **Locally sorry-free is not axiom-clean.**  Two `sorry`-bodied *instances* leak
29	  through typeclass synthesis: `instHasPicScheme`
30	  (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, the sole producer of `HasPicScheme`) and
31	  `pullback_preservesFiniteLimits`
32	  (`Cohomology/CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean`).  A theorem that merely
33	  *quantifies over* such a gate reports clean axioms, because the hypothesis is
34	  discharged by the caller; the leak appears at any call site that must
35	  synthesise the instance.  Run
36	  [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean) (`lake env lean
37	  scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`, ~12s warm) before believing any completeness
38	  claim — it measures the frontier rather than inferring it.
39	- 66 of the 172 modules still open with a bare `import Mathlib`; this is the
40	  dominant build cost and is being converted bottom-up with the helpers in
41	  `scripts/`.
42	
43	## Open decision
44	
45	Whether to represent the plain relative Picard functor while carrying a
46	`k`-rational-point hypothesis — strictly weaker than the challenge statement,
47	since such a curve need not have a rational point — or to étale-sheafify and drop
48	the hypothesis, is an open decision for the project owner (roadmap
49	`AJC.picrep.rational-point`).  Both branches are recorded in the blueprint's FGA
50	chapter and at the Lean leaf `hasRationalPoint_and_geometricallyIntegral`
51	(`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`); neither is assumed.
52	
53	Cones closed: `AJC.substrate`, `AJC.linebundle`, `AJC.grquot`, `AJC.cech`.
54	Cones open: `AJC.fbc` (flat base change, three leaves), `AJC.rr`, `AJC.picrep`
55	(Picard representability), `AJC.pic0av` (Pic⁰ is an abelian variety),
56	`AJC.albanese`.  Run `horizon roadmap list --focus AJC.jacobian` for the live tree
57	— the roadmap, not this file, is the authority on status.
58	
59	## Navigation
60	
61	- [`AlgebraicJacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian.lean): project import root.
62	- [`AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean`](AlgebraicJacobian/Jacobian.lean): the final
63	  Jacobian witness interface and assembly point.  The witness is built from
64	  `Pic⁰_{C/k}` and depends on five stated obligations: `Pic0.smooth` and
65	  `Pic0.proper` upstream, plus three named leaves stated there.
66	- [`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`](scripts/axiom-frontier.lean): the axiom-frontier
67	  probe, and the reachability measurement in its header.
68	- [`blueprint/web/index.html`](blueprint/web/index.html): generated mathematical blueprint.
69	- [`analogies/README.md`](analogies/README.md): index to the historical design notes.
70	- [`../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md`](../Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/README.md):
71	  the alternative Rebuild route.
72	
73	## Layout
74	
75	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/`: sheaf cohomology, the finite-cover Čech
76	  complex, higher direct images, and flat base change.
77	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/`: line bundles, relative Spec, the relative Picard
78	  functor, Grassmannians, Quot schemes, flattening stratification, and Picard
79	  identity components.
80	- `AlgebraicJacobian/Albanese/`: rigidity and extension of rational maps, plus the
81	  Albanese factorization.
82	- `AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/`: divisor and adelic Riemann–Roch infrastructure.
83	- `blueprint/src/chapters/`: the mathematical blueprint.
84	- `hgraph/`: the generated statement/declaration dependency graph.

88	- `informal/`, `memory/`, `analogies/`: campaign plans, durable notes, and
89	  historical design notes.  See each directory's own index.
90	- [`../../references/summary.md`](../../references/summary.md): shared source
91	  bibliography and retrieval notes.

103	does not apply every option from the lakefile's `[leanOptions]` — in particular
104	`maxSynthPendingDepth` — so a direct-file-only instance-synthesis failure can be an

===== AJC.jacobian.assembly | pending | Package the final Jacobian witness
Construct picardJacobianWitness from Picard representability, the Pic0 abelian-variety structure, dimension g, and the Albanese universal property; discharge the protected Jacobian interface.

===== AJC.jacobian.reachability | pending | Wire the headline to the infrastructure
Wire the headline to the infrastructure, and publish the true axiom frontier.

HEADLINE WIRING: DONE (run 0054, commit c7e7f5acc). picardJacobianWitness was a bare sorry in a file whose only project import was Genus.lean, so its transitive closure was 8 modules and nothing in the Picard/cohomology/Riemann-Roch/Albanese development was reachable from it. It is now built from Scheme.Pic0Scheme C, with four of six witness fields supplied directly by Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean (grpObj, proper, smooth, geometricallyIrreducible). Reachability 8 -> 96 modules. lake build of Jacobian + AbelJacobi green (8654 jobs).

REMAINING, now three named leaves in Jacobian.lean rather than one opaque sorry, each pinned at the strength the assembly consumes:
 - hasRationalPoint_and_geometricallyIntegral: geometric integrality needs only Smooth => GeometricallyReduced, absent from mathlib v4.31 but PROVED in the sibling AJCR (Curve/GeometricallyReduced.lean, mathlib-generality, upstreaming candidate) -- a portable brick. The k-rational point does NOT follow from the challenge hypotheses; this is where the I-0372 decision lands.
 - smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0: Pic0.smooth gives bare smoothness; the witness needs relative dimension genus C. Verified nothing upstream supplies the refinement.
 - isAlbanese_pic0: Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property covers only the algebraically closed, positive-genus case; the witness needs arbitrary k and every marked point, genus 0 included (Mumford section 4 rigidity).

AXIOM FRONTIER: published and reproducible at scripts/axiom-frontier.lean (lake env lean, ~12s warm, 51 declarations). The substantive finding is that 'axiom-clean' was being claimed for theorems that merely QUANTIFY over a sorry-bodied gate: Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible, Pic0.isSeparated and Pic0.locallyOfFiniteType report clean axioms as stated, but pick up sorryAx as soon as a call site must synthesise HasPicScheme, whose sole producer instHasPicScheme is sorry-bodied. Three leakProbe_* declarations force that synthesis so the leak is measured, not inferred. Same for pullback_preservesFiniteLimits, which taints PreservesFiniteLimits for flat pullback even along an identity. Genuinely clean, measured: the whole adelic genus lane (Adelic.instModuleFiniteHModuleOne, chi_unit_eq_one_sub_genus, h1_unit_eq_genus, hModuleOneEquivH1Cok_curve), degree-1 affine vanishing, and cech_computes_higherDirectImage.

===== AJC.maintenance | active | Project quality and documentation
Maintain the ambitious AJC route through measured elaboration, warning and budget reduction, timeless blueprint prose, faithful pins, and reproducible build baselines. The dominant Cech hotspot and twelve bounded prose passes are closed. Open work is residual journal prose, 33 classified pin warnings, 734 print overflows plus 95 glyph notices, 162 Lean warning heads, 179 heartbeat-budget scopes, 20 depth overrides, umbrella-import review, and historical design-note consolidation.

===== AJC.maintenance.blueprint | pending | Blueprint prose and formalization pins

===== AJC.maintenance.blueprint.pins | pending | Lean-pin declaration audit
The current graph contains 1,913 blueprint nodes, 4,327 Lean nodes, 6,240 live nodes total, and 6,663 edges. It is stale-free, all uses edges topologically sort, and 33 classified unresolved-pin warnings remain.

Ten adjacent scopes in QuotScheme presentation descent remain candidates: five 2M command budgets paired with five 800k synthesis budgets. Equivalent pullback wrappers already shed similar scopes, but this target costs about 6:42 and has eleven direct consumers.

===== AJC.pic0av | pending | Pic^0 is an abelian variety (A.3)
Upgrade the Picard identity component to an abelian variety of dimension g. Open work is the cotangent and H1 dimension comparison, smoothness and properness, and the degree-zero point description.

===== AJC.pic0av.identity | pending | Identity component and degree-zero points
Construct the degree map, identify Pic0(k) with its kernel, and prove the dimension statement for the identity component.

===== AJC.pic0av.structure | pending | Smoothness, properness, and irreducibility
Prove Pic0 is smooth and proper; combine these with the completed geometric-irreducibility and group-object infrastructure to obtain the abelian-variety structure.

===== AJC.pic0av.tangent | pending | Cotangent space and H1 comparison

Represent the relative Picard functor by the Milne-Kollar route selected in informal/pic-representability-campaign.md: build Pic^r over a separably closed field from the h0=1 loci cut out by a tuple of rational points, glue, descend to k by a finite Galois quotient, then assemble the degrees by a coproduct. Open inputs on this route: the rigidified pushforward gate (AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward, held by task ajc-gate), uniform H1 vanishing and the chi-ledger (AJC.rr, held by ajc-rr), Div^d representability, the Milne glue, and Galois descent of rigidified classes.

Complete and sorry-free: Grassmannian representability, section graded rings and modules, Hilbert-Serre algebra, cell charts, and glue descent. The Nitsure Quot representability theorem remains under `AJC.picrep.quot`.

===== AJC.picrep.assembly | pending | Assemble the Picard scheme
Assemble the Picard scheme on the committed Milne-Kollar route: glue the h0=1 loci into Pic^r over a separably closed field (needs the 01JJ engine and a universe bridge, since picSharp is Type (u+1)-valued), spread the finite glue datum to a finite Galois level, descend picSharp points through rigidified pairs, and assemble the degree pieces as a coproduct over Z. Discharges instHasPicScheme (FGAPicRepresentability.lean:259), which is currently the sole producer of HasPicScheme and sorry-bodied, so its axioms leak by synthesis into every consumer (measured: scripts/axiom-frontier.lean).

Superseded description: this node previously read 'combine Quot representability and flattening stratification'. That was the Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route, which the tree marks off-path -- see AJC.picrep.

===== AJC.picrep.quot | pending | Nitsure Quot representability
OFF-PATH, retained not revived. Under projectivity, relative very ampleness and coherence, representability of the Quot functor from boundedness, the Grassmannian embedding, flattening stratification and closedness (Nitsure section 5). One open leaf: QuotRepresentability.lean:79.

This is the engine of the abandoned quotient endgame, not of the committed Milne-Kollar route (AJC.picrep). It is kept because the surrounding Grassmannian, graded-algebra and flattening substrate is sorry-free, genuinely reusable, and imported by the committed route; only this node's own leaf and AJC.picrep.serre are exclusive to the endgame. Do not build new consumers against HasSmoothProperQuotient.

===== AJC.picrep.quotbasechange | done | Quot base change and support
Sorry-free. Flat base change for the Quot construction and base change of the support of a quotient; these are the inputs the Nitsure representability endgame consumes. Modules: Picard/QuotFlatBaseChange, Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange, and the quasi-coherent descent machinery of Picard/QuotScheme.

===== AJC.picrep.rational-point | blocked | DECISION: the rational-point hypothesis
Needs a human decision. references/challenge.lean declares Jacobian C with no rational-point binder, but instHasPicScheme (Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:316) makes [HasRationalPoint C] an essential hypothesis -- correctly so, since without a section Pic(C x_k T)/pi_T^* Pic(T) need not be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman's theorem needs no section because it represents the ETALE sheaf. This was assumed to be a platform limitation, but mathlib v4.31 does have the etale topology (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean:32-50), so it is a design choice. Either etale-sheafify the Picard functor, or accept a theorem strictly weaker than the challenge statement. Nothing above this on the Picard path is safe until it is settled.

===== AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward | active | Rigidified pushforward engine (gate factored into four named leaves)
GATE FACTORED (run 0053). HasRigidPushforward is now four exactly-stated leaves that are machine-checked to compose: Picard/RigidPushforwardGate.lean, hasRigidPushforward_of_leaves. (1) IsIntegral (P^1_k) -- integrality of the projective line over the ONE field k; this alone discharges the whole Serre-finiteness anchor hH0 at every finitely generated k-algebra A (Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Constants.lean, p1Cech_h0_fg_of_isIntegral), replacing the previous A-indexed family of anchors. GeometricallyIntegral is also plumbed and is strictly stronger; it reduces further to the integral model Proj Z[X0,X1]. (2) P1CechFibrewiseBridge -- fibrewise Cech H1-vanishing at scheme points implies d tensor kappa(m) surjective at maximal ideals. (3) P1PushforwardLocalFreenessBridge -- the engine module conclusion implies p_*M locally free of rank fiberH0. (4) RigidPushforwardBaseChange -- the second gate field, zero infrastructure: every IsIso result for the adjoint mate in this tree needs [IsAffineHom f] and q is proper, so the entire content of the field is the non-affine case, and there is no composition/pasting API for pushforwardBaseChangeMap. CORRECTIONS: HasFiniteMapToP1 is NOT an open gate (it synthesizes for an AJC curve, sorry-free, clean axioms); and HasRigidPushforward has ZERO consumers anywhere in the workspace, so it is a prerequisite for future DivFamily work rather than a live blocker.

===== AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward.basechange | pending | The baseChange gate field -- non-affine cohomology and base change
Scheme.RigidPushforwardBaseChange (Picard/RigidPushforward.lean:342) is the second field of HasRigidPushforward and has NO infrastructure. Established by recon plus an adversarial re-verification: the tree's only IsIso theorems for the adjoint mate pushforwardBaseChangeMap are isIso_pushforwardBaseChangeMap_of_isPullback (Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer.lean:1108) and its chart form (:949), both requiring [IsAffineHom f] [IsAffineHom f']; with IsAffineHom q assumed the gate field closes in ONE line (probe-verified: the pinned pullback.condition is defeq to IsPullback.of_hasPullback's h.w, IsAffineHom f' follows by base-change stability, and the only residual obligation L.IsQuasicoherent comes from hL.isFinitePresentation). So the entire content of the field is the non-affine case for q : C_A -> Spec A. Two further obstacles: (a) there is NO composition/pasting API for pushforwardBaseChangeMap anywhere (no _comp, no pasting-of-squares lemma), so the natural route 'reduce along the finite affine pi_A : C_A -> P^1_A, then handle p : P^1_A -> Spec A' cannot be assembled even once the second half exists; (b) the only non-affine base-change iso in the tree, canonicalBaseChangeMap_isIso (Picard/QuotScheme.lean:6104), is about a DIFFERENT mate (built from the pullback 2-iso, not the unit; probe-verified not defeq) and assumes [Flat g], which this statement explicitly refuses. Cohomology/FlatBaseChange.lean:689 records the mate vs cancelBaseChange coherence as a known unresolved wall. The module-level input IS available: kerBaseChange bijective for EVERY base algebra, the fourth conclusion of p1Cech_h0_baseChange_of_fibrewise_h1_vanishing. Missing is the sheaf-level bridge, estimated 4-5 new bricks.

===== AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward.p1integral | pending | IsIntegral P^1_k -- the last H0-finiteness leaf
The whole B3 H0 anchor (finite generation of the Cech H0 of a finitely presented module on P^1_A, classically Serre finiteness) now rests on one statement: IsIntegral (P^1_k), integrality of the projective line over the single field k. Proved consequence chain (Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Constants.lean section 5): IsIntegral + IsProper implies Gamma(P^1_k,O) finite over k by mathlib finite_appTop_of_universallyClosed; qcqs H0 flat base change over a field carries that finiteness to Gamma(P^1_A,O) over A; the sheaf-gluing anchor fg_ker_ringSectionDiffBase_of_module_finite_top then gives hS0 and the Serre devissage of P1SectionsFinite gives hH0. The load-bearing sub-probe identified by two independent passes is the chart-ring identification: injectivity of Polynomial R into HomogeneousLocalization.Away (homogeneousSubmodule (ULift (Fin 2)) R) (X 0). The project has the surjectivity/spanning half only (span_p1CoordAway_pow_top, RiemannRoch/Adelic/P1ChartData.lean:265); RelLaurentChartData supplies spanning, never a basis, so any 'x-degree' argument is unsound without it. Write it Away.mk-first in the style of P1ChartData.lean:184-265 to dodge the val_injective isDefEq blowup. Landing the chart iso also yields IsReduced and IrreducibleSpace of P^1 by transport from mathlib's affine-space instances.

1	\chapter{The Quot scheme}
2	\label{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}
3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/QuotScheme.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/GradedHilbertSerre.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/HilbertPolynomial.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/ProjectiveSpace.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/SerreTwist.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/ProjectiveMorphism.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/SerreFiniteness.lean
4	
5	% STRATEGY NOTE. This chapter packages the Quot-foundations layer of the
6	% Grothendieck--Altman--Kleiman Quot-scheme construction
7	% \(\mathrm{Quot}^{\Phi,L}_{E/X/S}\): the per-fiber Hilbert polynomial, the
8	% Quot functor of \(T\)-flat coherent quotients of \(E_T\) on
9	% \(X_T = X \times_S T\), and the Grassmannian \emph{scheme} together with
10	% its representability. The Quot functor underlies the relative Picard
11	% functor via the Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\)
12	% -- the case \(E = \mathcal{O}_X\) of the Quot functor.
13	%
14	% LOAD-BEARING SUB-PREREQUISITE. The Quot construction embeds Quot as a
15	% locally closed subfunctor of a Grassmannian
16	% \(\mathrm{Grass}(W \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S} \mathrm{Sym}^r V, \Phi(r))\).
17	% Mathlib (at the pinned commit) carries no Grassmannian \emph{scheme} -- only
18	% a linear-algebra Grassmannian as a finite-rank-quotient variety. The
19	% scheme-level Grassmannian over an arbitrary noetherian base is therefore an
20	% in-project sub-build. This chapter introduces it as
21	% \cref{def:grassmannian_scheme} and states its representability
22	% (\cref{thm:grassmannian_representable}).
23	
24	\section{Setup and motivation}
25	\label{sec:quot_setup}
26	
27	Throughout this chapter, let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme, \(\pi : X \to S\) a
28	projective morphism, \(L\) a relatively very ample line bundle on \(X\) over \(S\),
29	and \(E\) a coherent sheaf on \(X\). The Quot construction packages the
30	\(T\)-flat coherent quotients \(E_T \twoheadrightarrow \mathcal{F}\) of the
31	pull-back \(E_T\) to \(X_T = X \times_S T\), modulo the equivalence
32	\(\langle \mathcal{F}, q\rangle = \langle \mathcal{F}', q'\rangle\) defined by
33	\(\ker(q) = \ker(q')\). Fixing the Hilbert polynomial

1	\chapter{FGA representability of the Picard scheme}
2	\label{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}
3	% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean
4	
5	\section{Setup and motivation}
6	\label{sec:fga_pic_setup}
7	
8	Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
9	integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
10	Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
11	\cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
12	set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
13	\'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
14	\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
15	representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
16	packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.
17	
18	\medskip
19	
20	\textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
21	constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
22	different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.
23	
24	The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
25	Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
26	as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
27	relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
28	(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
29	Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
30	\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
31	relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. This is the route
32	of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and its proof below.
33	
34	The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
35	separably closed field, from the open loci
36	\[
37	  C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
38	\]
39	cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
40	points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
41	before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
42	pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
43	classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme.
44	
45	The decisive difference is the quotient step. Altman--Kleiman descent needs
46	quasi-projectivity of the scheme being quotiented, which is not expressible in
47	the formalisation at present and without which the lemma is false
48	(\cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}); the Milne--Koll\'ar route takes
49	only finite Galois quotients under an orbit-in-affine hypothesis, and so avoids
50	that obstruction entirely. The Lean development therefore pursues the
51	Milne--Koll\'ar route. The quotient-route material below is retained as the
52	mathematics it is --- the divisor and Hilbert-scheme substrate it rests on is
53	consumed by both routes --- and is not the path currently being formalised.
54	
55	\medskip
56	
57	\textbf{Comparison with the sheafified Picard functor.} Kleiman \S 4 represents
58	the \'etale-sheafified functor \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\). This chapter instead
59	works throughout under the standing hypothesis that \emph{\(C\) has a
60	\(k\)-rational point} (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and states
61	representability against the \emph{plain} relative Picard functor
62	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp}. This is justified by
63	Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 (\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section
64	and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes
65	(automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and
66	base change), then the comparison maps
67	\[
68	  \Pic_{X/S}(T) \longrightarrow \Pic_{(X/S)\et}(T) \longrightarrow
69	  \Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(T)
70	\]
71	are bijective for every \(T\). Hence under the rational-point hypothesis the
72	plain relative functor \emph{is} the \'etale sheaf, so the rational point
73	allows us to work directly with \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
74	
75	The hypothesis is not a convenience: without a section the plain functor is not
76	even a Zariski sheaf in general, so a representability statement for
77	\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with no rational point would be false. Two honest
78	formulations are therefore available, and they prove different theorems.
79	
80	\begin{enumerate}
81	  \item Represent \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) and carry \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a
82	    hypothesis. This is the formulation of
83	    \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and of every representability assertion
84	    in this chapter. It is strictly weaker than a statement about all smooth
85	    proper geometrically integral curves, since such a curve need not have a
86	    rational point --- a conic without rational points, or a genus-\(2\) curve
87	    over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point, satisfies every other
88	    hypothesis.
89	  \item Represent the \'etale sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) and drop the
90	    rational point. This is Kleiman's own formulation, and needs no section
91	    precisely because sheafifying supplies \'etale-locally what the section
92	    would have supplied globally. It requires developing the Picard functor on
93	    the \'etale site.
94	\end{enumerate}
95	
96	Which formulation the project should target is a decision about what theorem is
97	being claimed, not a limitation of the platform. The two are recorded here
98	side by side; the chapter as written realises the first.
99	
100	Every representability assertion of this chapter accordingly carries the
101	rational-point hypothesis. A pointed curve \((C,P)\), as in
102	\cref{chap:AbelJacobi}, supplies such a section.
103

218	\section{The FGA representability theorem}
219	\label{sec:fga_pic_representability}
220	
221	We now state and prove the specialisation of Grothendieck's existence theorem
222	for the Picard scheme, in the specialisation needed for the Jacobian:
223	\(S = \Spec k\), \(X = C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral
224	curve. The general theorem (Kleiman \S 4, Thm.~4.8) covers any
225	\(X/S\) projective Zariski-locally over \(S\), flat, with integral geometric
226	fibers; we record the general statement and then specialise.
227	
228	\begin{theorem}[FGA representability of the Picard scheme]\leanok
229	  \label{thm:fga_pic_representability}
230	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.representable}
231	  \uses{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence, lem:smooth_proper_quotient,

233	        cor:flattening_stratification_curve, def:pic_sharp_representable,

235	  % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4, Main Thm.~th:main,

240	  % and \begin{sbscor}\label{cor:algsch}\end{sbscor}.
241	  \textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4, Main Thm.~4.8
242	  + Cor.~4.18.3.}
243	  Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral curve
244	  over \(k\) \emph{with a \(k\)-rational point}
245	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}). Then the relative Picard functor
246	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp} --- which under the
247	  rational-point hypothesis coincides with its \'etale sheafification
248	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), by Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 --- is representable by a
249	  \(k\)-scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\), separated and locally of finite type over
250	  \(k\), which is a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
251	  \(k\)-subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective
252	  subschemes. The scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\) is called the \emph{Picard scheme}
253	  of \(C/k\).
254	\end{theorem}
255	
256	\begin{proof}
257	  
258	  We follow Kleiman~\S 4, Thm.~4.8, specialised to \(S = \Spec k\) and
259	  \(X = C\). The proof proceeds in four conceptual steps, preceded by a
260	  comparison step; the underlying algebraic engine is the Quot scheme of
261	  \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme} and the relative Picard functor of
262	  \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}, together with the line-bundle / Quot
263	  correspondence of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}.
264	
265	  \emph{Step 0: reduce to the \'etale sheaf via the rational point.}
266	  By Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5, since \(C \to \Spec k\) has a section
267	  (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and \(\mathcal O_T = \pi_{T*}
268	  \mathcal O_{C \times_k T}\) holds for every \(k\)-scheme \(T\) (cohomology
269	  and base change for the proper geometrically integral fibers of
270	  \(C\times_k T/T\)), the comparison map
271	  \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T) \to \Pic_{(C/k)\et}(T)\) is bijective for all
272	  \(T\). It therefore suffices to represent the \'etale sheaf
273	  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), which is what Kleiman's theorem produces; the same
274	  scheme then represents \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
275	
276	  \emph{Step 1: stratify by Hilbert polynomial.}
277	  For each polynomial \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\), let \(P^\phi \subseteq
278	  \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) be the \'etale subsheaf whose \(T\)-points are
279	  represented by invertible sheaves \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) with
280	  \(\chi(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t^{-1}(n)) = \phi(n)\) for all \(t \in T\) (the
281	  Hilbert polynomial relative to the chosen polarisation
282	  \(\mathcal{O}_C(1)\) on the projective curve \(C\)). The \(P^\phi\) form a
283	  disjoint open cover of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) (openness via Kleiman's
284	  flat-base-change argument, \cref{lem:cech_flat_base_change} / Stacks Tag 02KH;
285	  cf.\ EGA III 7.9.11). It suffices to
286	  represent each \(P^\phi\) by an increasing union of open quasi-projective
287	  \(k\)-schemes.
288	
289	  \emph{Step 2: bound twists by \(m\)-regularity.}
290	  Given \(\phi\), fix \(m\) large enough that the \(T\)-points of \(P^\phi\) are
291	  representable by \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) satisfying
292	  \(R^i \pi_{T*} \mathcal{L}(n) = 0\) for all \(i \ge 1\), \(n \ge m\). Twisting
293	  by \(\mathcal{O}_C(m)\) defines an automorphism of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
294	  that carries \(P^\phi\) to \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) for \(\phi_0(n) := \phi(m + n)\).
295	  Hence it suffices to represent each \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) by a quasi-projective
296	  \(k\)-scheme.
297	
298	  \emph{Step 3: factor through the Abel map.}
299	  Consider the Abel map \(A_{C/k} : \mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
300	  of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}. The source \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
301	  is representable by an open subscheme of \(\Hilb_{C/k}\) (and hence by an
302	  open subscheme of the Quot scheme of \cref{thm:quot_representable}), and
303	  is quasi-projective over \(k\). Pulling back along
304	  \(P^{\phi_0}_0 \hookrightarrow \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) yields an open
305	  subscheme \(Z := P^{\phi_0}_0 \times_{\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}} \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)
306	  of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), which is again quasi-projective. The projection
307	  \(\alpha : Z \to P^{\phi_0}_0\) is a surjection of \'etale sheaves:
308	  given a \(T\)-point \(\lambda\) of \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) represented by an \'etale
309	  cover \(T' \to T\) and an invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{L}'\) on \(C \times_k
310	  T'\) with \(H^1(C_{t'}, \mathcal{L}'_{t'}) = 0\), the projective bundle
311	  \(\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{Q}) \to T'\) associated to

\section{Assembly: \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is an abelian variety}
\label{sec:pic0_isAbelianVariety}

A \(k\)-group scheme is an \emph{abelian variety} iff its underlying
\(k\)-scheme is a complete (proper) connected group variety
(Milne~\S I.1, p.~8). Combining the smoothness, properness, and
geometric irreducibility statements of this chapter with the
identity-component group-scheme structure of
\cref{chap:Picard_IdentityComponent} packages \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) as an
abelian variety of dimension \(g\). This is the load-bearing A.3.vii
gate for Route~A.

`Z := X ∖ U`. The codimension-`≥ 2` indeterminacy theorem for rational maps
into a complete variety gives `codim Z ≥ 2`; the pure-codimension-`1`
indeterminacy lemma for maps into a group variety says `Z` is empty or of pure
codimension `1`. Both together force `Z = ∅`, so `U = X` and `f` has a regular
representative on all of `X`. Uniqueness is the agreement principle
`AlgebraicGeometry.ext_of_isDominant`: two morphisms `X ⟶ A` out of a reduced
scheme into a separated scheme that agree on a dense open agree everywhere. -/

/-- **A scheme smooth over an algebraically closed field is reduced**
(Stacks `056S`/`033B` over `k̄`). Used to derive `IsReduced A.left` in
`av_isIntegral_of_smooth_geomIrred` below.

The proof is `isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed` in
`Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean`: the stalks are localisations of
standard-smooth `k̄`-algebras, whose localisations at maximal ideals are
regular local hence domains, and reducedness is checked at those maximal
localisations and then transported to the stalks. Algebraic closure of `k̄` is
genuinely used. -/
private theorem isReduced_of_smooth_over_field
    {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
    (A : Over (Spec (.of kbar)))
    [Smooth A.hom] :
    IsReduced A.left :=
  isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed A

/-- **An abelian variety has integral underlying scheme.** For an abelian
variety `A` over an algebraically closed field `k̄` — an object
`A : Over (Spec (.of k̄))` carrying
`[GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom]` —
the scheme `A.left` is integral.

Three steps:

1. `Spec k̄` is a one-point scheme.
2. Geometric irreducibility of `A.hom` over a one-point base gives
   `IrreducibleSpace A.left`
   (`GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton`).

\label{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}
% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean

% relative Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of
% \cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} (A.1.b) to its abelian-group-valued

% It \emph{gates} A.2.c (\cref{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}) since
% Grothendieck's existence theorem represents precisely the \'etale-sheafified
% functor (cf.\ [Kleiman], \S 4, th:main: ``\dots represents
% \(\Pic_{(X/S)\et}\).''). It is \emph{not} responsible for representability
% (that is A.2.c) and not responsible for the identity-component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\)
% (that is A.3).

% NOTE (planner directive iter-174). Per the iter-174 plan, the chapter has

\section{Setup and motivation}
\label{sec:relpic_setup}

Fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically integral curve \(C\) over
\(k\). As in \cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback}, write
\(\pi_T : C \times_k T \to T\) for the projection of a relative curve over a
    plus-construction
    \texttt{CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.sheafify}) with the

    PicSharp.presheaf} under the forgetful functor, using
    \texttt{CategoryTheory.GrothendieckTopology.sheafification\_obj}
    (the equality \(\texttt{J.sheafification D}.\mathrm{obj}\, P =
    \texttt{J.sheafify}\, P\)) and the fact that the forgetful functor

    multiequalizer / filtered-colimit data used by the
    plus-construction (\texttt{plusPlusSheaf} commutes with

\end{itemize}

The relationship with \cref{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability} is captured by
the slogan: the FGA Picard scheme of A.2.c represents
\(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) (Kleiman \S 4, the main existence theorem: ``\dots represents
\(\Pic_{(X/S)\et}\)''), \emph{not} \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) directly. The \'etale
sheafification step of this chapter is precisely what makes the
representability theorem in A.2.c well-posed.

\section{Out of scope}
\label{sec:relpic_out_of_scope}

The following constructions are downstream of this chapter and live in

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Representability of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) by a scheme}

\section{Setup and motivation}
\label{sec:relspec_setup}

The Route~A construction of \(J = \Pic^0_{C/k}\) as a \(g\)-dimensional abelian variety is
organised around the relative Picard functor
\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T) = \Pic(C \times_k T) / \pi_T^* \Pic(T)\)
on the category of \(k\)-schemes. Representing \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) requires the line-bundle
pullback construction on a relative curve \(C \times_k T \to T\), which in turn rests on a
\emph{relative scheme} construction on a quasi-coherent sheaf of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-algebras
\(\mathcal{A}\), the \emph{relative spectrum}
\(\pi : \underline{\Spec}_X(\mathcal{A}) \to X\). This chapter packages the construction
of \(\underline{\Spec}_X(-)\) and its three core properties --- universal property, affine
base, base change --- as the foundational A.1.a building block. The relative Picard
functor itself (A.1.c), the line-bundle pullback functor on a product (A.1.b), and the
identity-component / dimension theory of \(J\) (A.3) live in separate sibling chapters
devoted to those constructions.

\section{Quasi-coherent sheaves of algebras}
\label{sec:qc_sheaf_of_algebras}

\begin{definition}[Quasi-coherent \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-algebra]

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

/-! ## §0.0. Substrate bridges: geometric integrality and rational points

`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` states `Pic⁰_{C/k}` smooth,
proper and geometrically irreducible under the hypotheses
`[GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C]
[PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]`, whereas the Albanese curve `C`
enters here carrying only `[SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
[GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]` over an algebraically closed field `k̄`. The
three bridging facts below discharge the missing hypotheses, so that
`Pic0.bundle` can be assembled from the upstream declarations. -/

/-- **Reducedness descends along a faithfully flat morphism.** If `π : Y ⟶ X` is
flat and surjective (i.e. faithfully flat) and `Y` is reduced, then `X` is
reduced: each stalk map `𝒪_{X,π(y)} → 𝒪_{Y,y}` is a flat local homomorphism of
local rings, hence faithfully flat and in particular injective, so `𝒪_{X,π(y)}`
embeds into the reduced ring `𝒪_{Y,y}`. -/
theorem isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (π : Y ⟶ X)
    [Flat π] [Surjective π] [IsReduced Y] : IsReduced X := by
  haveI hst : ∀ x : X, _root_.IsReduced (X.presheaf.stalk x) := by
    intro x
    obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := π.surjective x
    have hlocal : IsLocalHom (π.stalkMap y).hom := inferInstance
    have hflat : (π.stalkMap y).hom.Flat := Flat.stalkMap π y
    have hinj : Function.Injective (π.stalkMap y).hom := by
      algebraize [(π.stalkMap y).hom]
      haveI : Module.Flat (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) := hflat
      haveI : IsLocalHom (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) := hlocal
      haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat (X.presheaf.stalk (π.base y)) (Y.presheaf.stalk y) :=
        Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_flat_of_isLocalHom
      exact FaithfulSMul.algebraMap_injective _ _
    exact isReduced_of_injective (π.stalkMap y).hom hinj
  exact isReduced_of_isReduced_stalk X

/-- **A scheme smooth over an algebraically closed field is geometrically
reduced.** For each test field `K/k̄`, the base change `X ×_{k̄} K` is smooth
over `K`; its further base change to `K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K` is smooth over an
algebraically closed field, hence reduced
(`Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed`), and reducedness descends along the
faithfully flat projection `X_{K̄} → X_K` (`isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective`). -/
theorem geometricallyReduced_of_smooth {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of kbar)) [Smooth f] :
    GeometricallyReduced f := by
  refine ⟨?_⟩
  rw [geometrically_iff_of_commRing_of_isClosedUnderIsomorphisms]
  intro K _ _
  have hfsurj : (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))).hom.FaithfullyFlat :=
    RingHom.faithfullyFlat_algebraMap_iff.mpr inferInstance
  have hFS := (flat_and_surjective_SpecMap_iff
    (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))).mpr hfsurj
  haveI : Flat (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))) := hFS.1
  haveI : Surjective (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))) := hFS.2
  haveI hsm1 : Smooth (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K)))) :=
    inferInstance
  haveI hsm2 : Smooth (pullback.snd
      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))) := inferInstance
  haveI : Smooth (Over.mk (pullback.snd
      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))).hom := hsm2
  haveI : IsReduced (pullback (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))) :=
    Scheme.isReduced_of_smooth_of_isAlgClosed (kbar := AlgebraicClosure K) (Over.mk (pullback.snd
      (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K))))))
  exact isReduced_of_flat_of_surjective
    (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap kbar K))))
      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K (AlgebraicClosure K)))))

/-- **A smooth, geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically closed
field has a rational point.** `C.left` is nonempty (geometric irreducibility over
the one-point base `Spec k̄`), locally of finite type over `k̄` (smoothness) and
therefore a Jacobson space, so it has a closed point `x`; over the algebraically
closed field `k̄`, `pointOfClosedPoint`/`pointEquivClosedPoint` promote `x` to a
`k̄`-rational section of `C.hom`. This discharges `[HasRationalPoint C]`. -/
theorem hasRationalPoint_of_isAlgClosed {kbar : Type u} [Field kbar] [IsAlgClosed kbar]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of kbar))) [Smooth C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
    Scheme.HasRationalPoint C := by
  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom := inferInstance
  haveI : IrreducibleSpace C.left :=
    GeometricallyIrreducible.irreducibleSpace_of_subsingleton C.hom
  haveI : JacobsonSpace C.left := LocallyOfFiniteType.jacobsonSpace C.hom
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := nonempty_inter_closedPoints (X := C.left) (Z := Set.univ)
    Set.univ_nonempty isClosed_univ.isLocallyClosed
  exact ⟨⟨(pointEquivClosedPoint C.hom).symm ⟨x, hx.2⟩⟩⟩

/-!
# FGA representability of the Picard scheme

This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).

The relative Picard functor is

```
picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
```

the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
against it is a natural bijection
`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.

## The étale-sheafification route: Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5

Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`.
Mathlib at the pinned revision has no étale Grothendieck topology on
schemes, so instead of sheafifying we use Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: when
`f : X → S` has a **section** and `O_S = f_* O_X` holds universally (true
for our proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparison maps

```
Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
```

are all **bijective**. Hence, under a `k`-rational-point hypothesis
(`HasRationalPoint C` below), the *plain* relative functor `picSharp C` is
itself representable, and the FGA statement can be made against it directly
— no étale topology needed. Without a section the plain functor is not
representable in general (it need not even be a Zariski sheaf), which is why
representability is asserted only **conditionally on `[HasRationalPoint C]`**:
an unconditional statement would be false. For the same reason `picSharp` may
not be wired to the *absolute* functor `PicSharp.presheaf`.

## Main results

* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
  quotient encoding).
* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
  scheme and the natural bijection
  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.

## Remaining obligations

One statement in this file is still `sorry`: `instHasPicScheme`, the existence
of a scheme that represents `picSharp C` and is separated and locally of
finite type over `k`, given a rational point. Mathematically this is Kleiman
§4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`, transported through §2
Thm 2.5. Everything else here — in particular representability of the chosen
scheme, its local finiteness, its separatedness, and its group-scheme
structure — is derived from that one existence statement.

`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.

## References

Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.
Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020): §2 Thm 2.5
(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
-/

807	\section{Dependencies of the representability theorem}
808	\label{sec:fga_pic_sorry_closure_order}
809	
810	The construction of \(\Pic_{C/k}\) separates into three mathematical inputs:
811	the relative-divisor functor, its Abel map to the relative Picard functor, and
812	the FGA existence theorem. The first two supply concrete functors and a
813	natural transformation. The third combines them with regularity, cohomology
814	and base change, and effective descent to produce a scheme locally of finite
815	type representing \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
816	
817	\subsection{The Picard-scheme existence theorem}
818	\label{subsec:sorry_has_pic_scheme}
819	
820	For a
821	smooth proper geometrically integral curve \(C/k\) with a \(k\)-rational
822	point, the relative Picard functor \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\)
823	(\cref{def:pic_sharp_carrier}) is representable by a \(k\)-scheme. The
824	proof first applies Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5, using the section to identify the
825	plain functor with its \'etale sheafification, and then uses Kleiman's four
826	steps
827	(\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}): Hilbert-polynomial stratification,
828	\(m\)-regularity bound, Abel-map factorisation through
829	\(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), and the smooth-proper quotient
830	(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}). Its inputs are the Quot/Hilbert
831	construction of \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, representability of
832	\(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) as in \cref{rem:div_functor_representability}, the
833	regularity result \cref{cor:flattening_stratification_curve}, the base-change
834	result \cref{lem:cech_flat_base_change}, and Altman--Kleiman effective descent.
835	The resulting representing object gives
836	natural bijections
837	\[
838	  (T\to\Pic_{C/k})\simeq
839	  \Pic(C\times_kT)/\pi_T^*\Pic(T),
840	\]
841	including the dual-number case \(T=\Spec k[\epsilon]\) used in the
842	tangent-space calculation.
843	
844	\subsection{The relative-divisor input}
845	\label{subsec:sorry_has_div_functor}
846	
847	The relative-divisor functor \(\Div_{X/S}\) of
848	\cref{def:div_functor} is the subfunctor of the Hilbert functor
849	\(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of relative effective Cartier
850	divisors, in the invertible-kernel quotient encoding of

\chapter{Flattening Stratification of a Coherent Sheaf}
\label{chap:Picard_FlatteningStratification}

\section{Setup and motivation}
\label{sec:flatstrat_setup}

The construction of the Quot scheme \(\Quot_{\F/X/S}^{\Phi,L}\) in Nitsure's exposition
of Grothendieck's existence theorem (\cite{nitsure-hilbert-quot}, \S5) proceeds by
embedding the functor of points of \(\Quot\) into a Grassmannian via Castelnuovo--Mumford
regularity, then cutting out the locus of \emph{quotients with flat fibres of the
prescribed Hilbert polynomial} by a closed-subscheme condition.  Cutting out this
locus uses, as a primary technical input, the existence of the
\emph{flattening stratification} of a coherent sheaf \(\F\) on a projective
\(S\)-scheme: a finite collection of locally-closed subschemes of \(S\) on each of which
the restriction of \(\F\) becomes flat.

We work throughout with a noetherian base scheme \(S\), a projective morphism
\(\pi : X \to S\), and a coherent \(\OO_X\)-module \(\F\). The conclusion of Nitsure's
theorem covers an arbitrary noetherian base with a projective \(X \to S\), which
applies in particular to \(X = C \times_k T\), where \(C\) is a smooth proper
curve over a field \(k\), \(T\) is a noetherian \(k\)-scheme, and \(\F\) is a
coherent sheaf on the relative curve.

\label{chap:Picard_GrassmannianQuot}

The previous chapter constructed the Grassmannian scheme \(\mathrm{Gr}(r,d)\) over
\(\mathbb{Z}\) by gluing the affine charts \(U^I\)
(\cref{def:gr_affine_chart}) along the transition isomorphisms
(\cref{def:gr_transition}) satisfying the cocycle condition
(\cref{lem:gr_cocycle}), and proved that the structure morphism
\(\mathrm{Gr}(r,d) \to \Spec \mathbb{Z}\) is separated (\cref{lem:gr_separated})

\(U^I_J \subseteq U^I\).

\chapter{The Grassmannian over $\mathbb{Z}$: affine charts and gluing}
\label{chap:Picard_GrassmannianCells}

\section{Set-up: charts indexed by $d$-subsets}
\label{sec:gr_setup}

Fix integers \(r \ge d \ge 1\). For a \(d \times r\) matrix \(M\) over a ring
and a subset \(I \subseteq \{1, \dots, r\}\) with \(\#(I) = d\), write \(M_I\)
for the \emph{\(I\)-th minor} of \(M\): the \(d \times d\) submatrix whose
columns are those indexed by \(I\). We construct the Grassmannian scheme
\(\mathrm{Gr}(r,d)\) over \(\mathbb{Z}\) by gluing one affine chart \(U^I\) for
each such \(I\). The construction is, conceptually, the quotient
\(\mathrm{GL}_{d,\mathbb{Z}} \backslash V\) of the scheme \(V\) of rank-\(d\)
matrices, but we never use the language of group-scheme actions: the charts and
their transition maps are elementary matrix algebra over \(\mathbb{Z}\). Taking
\(d = 1\) recovers \(\mathrm{Gr}(r,1) = \mathbb{P}^{r-1}_{\mathbb{Z}}\).

\chapter{Effective descent: restriction of the glued sheaf to a chart}
\label{chap:Picard_GlueDescent}

\providecommand{\ShMod}{\mathrm{SheafOfModules}}

The gluing primitive \cref{def:scheme_modules_glue} produces, out of a glue datum
\(D\) of schemes (index set \(J\), charts \(U_i\), overlaps \(V_{ij}\), overlap
immersions \(f_{ij} : V_{ij} \hookrightarrow U_i\), transition isomorphisms
\(t_{ij} : V_{ij} \xrightarrow{\sim} V_{ji}\), glued scheme \(X\) with chart
immersions \(\iota_i : U_i \hookrightarrow X\)), a sheaf of \(\mathcal{O}_X\)-modules
\(\mathcal{M}\) as the descent equalizer
\[
  \mathcal{M} \;=\; \operatorname{eq}(a, b)
    \;\hookrightarrow\; \prod_{i} (\iota_i)_{*}\,\mathcal{M}_i
\]
of two parallel maps into the overlap product. That construction makes
\(\mathcal{M}\) but does \emph{not} yet consume the cocycle conditions (C1)/(C2) on
the transition family \((g_{ij})\). This chapter discharges the remaining content of
descent: it shows that restricting the glued sheaf back to a chart recovers the
input sheaf there. Concretely, the canonical \emph{restriction morphism}
\(\iota_i^{*}\mathcal{M} \to \mathcal{M}_i\) -- the adjoint transpose along the chart
immersion \(\iota_i\) of the \(i\)-th equalizer projection -- is an isomorphism, and
it is here that (C1)/(C2) are used. The engine is that pullback along an open
immersion is, up to natural isomorphism, the site-level restriction functor
(\cref{lem:modules_restrictFunctorIsoPullback_mathlib}); being a right adjoint it
preserves the descent equalizer and the pushforward product, so the chart
restriction of \(\mathcal{M}\) is computed factor by factor. The non-formal input is
the \emph{overlap base change} \(\beta_{ij}\), which identifies the restricted
pushforward factor \(\iota_i^{*}(\iota_j)_{*}\mathcal{M}_j\) with a pushforward of a
restriction of \(\mathcal{M}_j\) to the overlap, using the cartesianness of the

\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}

\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
[Representability of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)]
  \label{rem:div_functor_representability}
  Kleiman~\S 3, Thm.~th:repDiv, shows that \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) is
  representable by an open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \subseteq
  \Hilb_{C/k}\) of the Hilbert scheme (\(\Hilb_{C/k} =
  \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\), \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}): letting
  \(W \subseteq C \times_k \Hilb_{C/k}\) be the universal closed
  subscheme and \(q \colon W \to \Hilb_{C/k}\) the projection, the locus
  \(V \subseteq W\) where \(W\) is locally an effective Cartier divisor
  is open, so \(Z := q(W \setminus V)\) is closed (\(q\) proper) and
  \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} := \Hilb_{C/k} \setminus Z\) is the open
  subscheme representing relative effective divisors. This is
  the relative-divisor functor appearing in
  \cref{def:div_functor_carrier}.
  of \'etale sheaves, both \(Q\) and \(P\) are coequalisers of the pair
  \(R \rightrightarrows Z\); the coequaliser is unique up to unique
  isomorphism, so \(Q\) represents \(P\). Smoothness of \(\alpha : Z \to P\)
  is the smoothness of \(Z \to Q\) just shown.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Quasi-projectivity is load-bearing]
  \label{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}
  \uses{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}
  Hypothesis (ii) of \cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient} --- that \(Z\) be
  representable by a \emph{quasi-projective} \(k\)-scheme --- cannot be weakened
  to bare representability. A Hironaka-type free \(\mathbb{Z}/2\)-action on a
  smooth proper non-projective threefold gives a smooth proper equivalence
  relation satisfying (i), (iii) and (iv) whose quotient \'etale sheaf is an
  algebraic space and not a scheme.

  This is what separates the two routes of \cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}. The
  quotient route must supply quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice; the
  Milne--Koll\'ar route quotients only by a finite Galois group, under the
  hypothesis that every finite orbit lies in an affine open, which is a
  condition the Hironaka example fails.
\end{remark}

\label{sec:fga_pic_lean_encoding}

The constructions above fit together through the following interfaces. The
relative Picard presheaf is obtained from the quotient of invertible sheaves
on \(C\times_kT\) by pullbacks from \(T\), and its set-valued version is used
when applying representability. The relative-divisor functor is the
specialisation of the effective Cartier-divisor functor to
\(C\to\operatorname{Spec}k\). A divisor family \(\langle\mathcal F,q\rangle\)
is sent by the Abel map to the inverse class of its kernel:
\[
  \langle\mathcal F,q\rangle\longmapsto-[\ker q].
\]
The FGA theorem applies Hilbert-polynomial stratification, a regularity bound,
the Abel-map factorisation, and the smooth-proper quotient lemma. Tensor
product and dualisation of line bundles then induce addition and inversion on
the representing scheme.

\begin{itemize}
  \item The Picard scheme \cref{def:pic_scheme} is selected by the
    existence assertion \cref{def:has_pic_scheme}.
  \item The functor \cref{def:pic_sharp_carrier} is the set-valued form of
    the relative Picard presheaf of \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}.
  \item The Abel map of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence} is the natural
    transformation \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) sending a
    relative divisor family \(\langle \mathcal F, q\rangle\) to
    \(-[\ker q]\), the class of its associated invertible sheaf.
  \item The Altman--Kleiman lemma \cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient} gives
    descent of a flat-and-proper equivalence relation \(R \subseteq Z
    \times_k Z\) on a quasi-projective \(k\)-scheme \(Z\) to a
    quasi-projective quotient \(Q\) representing the coequalising sheaf.
  \item The theorem \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} supplies the
    representing scheme.
  \item Yoneda transport of the abelian-group structure on
    \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) gives the group-scheme structure of
    \cref{thm:pic_is_group_scheme}.
\end{itemize}

The effective-quotient theorem for flat and proper equivalence relations on
quasi-projective schemes is recorded as
\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}. All other interfaces are supplied by the
relative Picard, divisor, and Quot constructions.
